assertions.description: The WebTransport constructor exists (baseline for every other assertion in this suite — the hints extend it).
The constructor actually reads the anticipatedConcurrentIncomingUnidirectionalStreams dictionary member (observed via a getter, not inferred from prototype shape).
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; let read = false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { get anticipatedConcurrentIncomingUnidirectionalStreams() { read = true; return 42; } }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); try { t.close(); } catch {} } catch {} return read; })()

assertions.description: A hint passed to the constructor is stored and read back exactly through the instance attribute (400 in, 400 out).
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { anticipatedConcurrentIncomingUnidirectionalStreams: 400 }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); const got = t.anticipatedConcurrentIncomingUnidirectionalStreams; try { t.close(); } catch {} return got === 400; } catch { return false; } })()

assertions.description: The member is [EnforceRange] unsigned short: passing 65536 to the constructor throws a TypeError instead of wrapping or being ignored.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { anticipatedConcurrentIncomingUnidirectionalStreams: 65536 }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); try { t.close(); } catch {} return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: Passing -1 throws a TypeError — without [EnforceRange] a negative value would wrap to 65535.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { anticipatedConcurrentIncomingUnidirectionalStreams: -1 }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); try { t.close(); } catch {} return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: The type is nullable: constructing with the member set to null succeeds and the attribute reads back null (no hint), not 0.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { anticipatedConcurrentIncomingUnidirectionalStreams: null }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); const got = t.anticipatedConcurrentIncomingUnidirectionalStreams; try { t.close(); } catch {} return got === null; } catch { return false; } })()

assertions.description: The attribute is read-write: assigning a new in-range value on a live object is stored and read back (the mid-session raise the feature promises).
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function' || !('anticipatedConcurrentIncomingBidirectionalStreams' in WebTransport.prototype)) return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { anticipatedConcurrentIncomingBidirectionalStreams: 50 }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); t.anticipatedConcurrentIncomingBidirectionalStreams = 800; const got = t.anticipatedConcurrentIncomingBidirectionalStreams; try { t.close(); } catch {} return got === 800; } catch { return false; } })()
